sessions.title: Placing custom furniture in a 3D room

turns.requestSummary: How should I let someone place a made-to-measure cabinet in a scanned room without it drifting when the camera moves?

answer.title: Anchor the cabinet to the room, not the camera
answer.body:
Raycast from the pointer into the reconstructed room and store a [surface-local pose](zoom:surface-local-pose): hit position, surface normal, tangent direction, and the room-mesh identifier. Rebuild the cabinet's world transform from that pose on every frame.

Keep the preview translucent until the asset has a valid support surface. On commit, persist the local pose and cabinet dimensions—not the current camera-relative matrix. [Details](zoom:placement-pipeline)

surface-local-pose.title: Surface-local pose
surface-local-pose.content: A placement described relative to a specific piece of room geometry. It remains stable when the camera moves or its tracking estimate is refined.

placement-pipeline.title: Placement pipeline
placement-pipeline.content:
1. Cast a ray from the pointer through the camera.
2. Reject hits outside the floor or wall class allowed by the cabinet.
3. Build an orthonormal frame from the hit normal and a stable tangent.
4. Place the cabinet pivot at the hit point plus its configured clearance.
5. Save the mesh identifier and local transform when the user commits.

If the reconstructed mesh is replaced, remap the anchor to the closest compatible surface before falling back to world space.

turns.requestSummary: What should happen when the cabinet is rotated into a corner or overlaps skirting and sockets?

answer.title: Separate intentional alignment from invalid overlap
answer.body:
Snap yaw in small increments around the support normal, but keep a modifier or two-finger gesture for continuous rotation. A [clearance envelope](zoom:clearance-envelope) should include doors, drawers, ventilation, and installation space—not only the visible cabinet mesh.

Show the first blocking reason beside the preview and keep the last valid pose available for a one-step undo. Corners can attract the cabinet when both wall distances fall within a small, scale-aware threshold. [Details](zoom:collision-policy)

clearance-envelope.title: Clearance envelope
clearance-envelope.content: An invisible volume representing the space an object needs to operate and be installed. It may be larger than the rendered geometry.

collision-policy.title: Collision and snapping policy
collision-policy.content:
Evaluate constraints in a predictable order: support, room bounds, fixed obstacles, operational clearance, then optional alignment snaps. Treat sockets and vents as hard exclusions; treat nearby edges and corners as soft snap candidates.

Use hysteresis so a snap remains active until the pointer moves meaningfully beyond the entry threshold. This prevents the preview from flickering between snapped and free placement.

turns.requestSummary: Give me the smallest production-ready data contract so placements reopen consistently on desktop and AR devices.

answer.title: Persist intent, geometry identity, and a recoverable fallback
answer.body:
Store the asset version, parametric dimensions, anchor identifier, local transform, constraint state, and a world-space fallback. Add a [placement revision](zoom:placement-revision) so concurrent edits cannot silently overwrite one another.

On load, resolve the anchor first, reapply constraints, and then compare the reconstructed world pose with the fallback. If the difference exceeds your tolerance, ask the user to confirm the remap instead of moving the cabinet invisibly. [Details](zoom:placement-contract)

placement-revision.title: Placement revision
placement-revision.content: A monotonically increasing value attached to one saved placement. An update succeeds only when it is based on the current revision.

placement-contract.title: Minimal saved placement
placement-contract.content:
```json
{
  "assetVersion": "cabinet-oak@7",
  "dimensionsMm": [1200, 420, 900],
  "anchorId": "room-mesh:wall-18",
  "localMatrix": [16, "finite numbers"],
  "constraints": { "support": "floor", "cornerSnap": true },
  "fallbackWorldMatrix": [16, "finite numbers"],
  "revision": 12
}
```

Validate every numeric component before applying the transform. Keep asset migrations explicit so an updated cabinet model cannot reinterpret old dimensions without review.
